messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert — hosted-api region-us-east p95 > 1.5s and queue length > 10k. Auto-scale attempted but failed to add nodes. Paging oncall.

maya: I'm oncall, looking. seeing a huge POST spike since 18:02 UTC. p95 jumped from ~120ms to 1.8s in 2m, p99 ~9s. queue_depth: 12,400. GPU pools at 100% util.

maya: re-checking autoscaler logs now, linking what I see:
```
[autoscaler] 18:04:12 ERROR scale_up failed: quota.exceeded: Cannot allocate more GPUs in project
[autoscaler] 18:04:13 INFO current_replicas=48, desired=96, scaling_attempts=3
[hosted-queue] backlog=12400 inflight=3200 avg_latency_p95=1800ms p99=9200ms
```

ajay: @maya any sign of fallback routing? we should route to secondary region or older smaller model variants if available.

maya: fallback routing tried, but policy says "prefer same-region" and fallback pool also saturated. The policy didn't kick because model_variant compatibility check failed for some requests (long context).

sophia: Can we temporarily enforce token/frequency throttles at edge for top noisy API keys? Might reduce burst.

maya: yes, I'm running quick query to identify top keys by qps.

ops-bot: Top 5 API keys by QPS last 60s: key-A(28%), key-B(15%), key-C(9%), key-D(6%), key-E(4%).

maya: I'm going to apply a per-key limiter to key-A and key-B to 60% of current rate to reduce queue growth. Doing a rolling change now.

carlos: ETA for limiter rollout? post the command you use.

maya: running:
```sh
redwoodctl rate-limit set --key key-A --rate 120r/s --scope hosted-api --reason "emergency throttle due to queue growth"
redwoodctl rate-limit set --key key-B --rate 80r/s --scope hosted-api
```

maya: applied. watching.

(small pause)

maya: queue dropped to 8.6k after 30s, p95 down to 950ms. still high but trending.

ajay: good. we still need more capacity. can infra request extra quota from cloud? If quota is the blocker we should open an expedited request and meanwhile spin up reserved nodes in another AZ if possible.

liam: I can attempt cross-region burst: spin up 24 smaller gpus in us-west as emergency pool and modify routing to send 20% of traffic there. This will take ~6-8m to be ready. Need approval to override cost controls.

maya: approve. do it. add a high-priority tag and notify billing to expect emergency spend.

liam: kicking off provisioning. command:
```sh
infractl provision --region us-west --gpus a10x8 --count 24 --tag emergency-1919023456
```

ops-bot: Provision request accepted, estimate ready in 7m.

maya: meanwhile I'm enabling fallback to smaller quantized model variant (q4_2) for non-chat endpoints to reduce per-token GPU time. This may change output slightly but keeps service up. applying canary.

sophia: document customer impact: customers querying large contexts with chat streaming may see degraded quality or different tokenization. Also some requests may be timed out if they're queued past 30s. Need to notify support.

maya: creating incident ticket in zendesk now and posting to #support with recommended message.

maya: incident note:
"We are experiencing elevated request latency and timeouts in us-east due to a sudden traffic spike and exhausted GPU capacity. We have: applied emergency per-key rate limits for top noisy keys, enabled temporary fallback to smaller quantized model variants, and are provisioning emergency GPU capacity in us-west. Estimated mitigation in 8–10 minutes. We will follow up with root cause and timeline."

carlos: good. any customer-visible errors? 429s or 503s?

maya: 429s spiked right after limiter applied (expected). Prior to that customers were seeing 504 gateway timeouts and long streaming stalls. We replaced some long-poll handlers to return earlier status to clients to reduce connection buildup.

ajay: once us-west pool is ready, route only non-stateful, small-context requests there first to avoid compatibility issues. keep chat sessions in us-east for now.

liam: us-west pool ready in ~6m. I'll add pool to routing and start gradual 15% shift.

ops-bot: Routing update applied: us-west-emergency pool receives 15% of eligible requests.

maya: p95 now 420ms, queue 2.3k. p99 1.2s. This is much better.

sophia: great. set incident severity to Sev2, notify affected customers via support. Also start collecting logs for autoscaler failure (quota vs AZ scarcity).

maya: autoscaler failure root cause: cloud provider quota limits + one AZ had capacity shortage, autoscaler retried across AZs then failed with quota.exceeded. I'm capturing a timeline and will escalate to infra team to pre-warm capacity and request quota increase.

ajay: action items assigned:
- maya: keep throttles until traffic normalizes and then ramp down slowly.
- liam: coordinate with infra procurement to request quota bump and capacity reservations.
- sophia: draft customer comms and work with support.
- carlos: run perf tests to ensure q4_2 variant meets regressions for top customers.

carlos: will start regression evals now.

maya: handing off to @ajay for the overnight watch. I'm staying on to finish incident notes for 10 more minutes then stepping off.

ajay: taking over. thanks @maya for triage. I'll monitor charts and escalate if anything regresses.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged by ajay (oncall). Escalation path: infra oncall, paging list updated.

maya: post-incident followups: schedule postmortem in #postmortems, include: autoscaler improvements (better quota detection + cross-AZ fallback), routing policy improvements (allow immediate cross-region fallback for timeout-critical paths), and automated noisy-key throttles (non-manual).

ajay: noted. I'll add runbook updates and a short blameless timeline.

sophia: posting initial customer message in #support: "We're mitigating elevated latency across hosted API in us-east; temporary rate limits applied for a subset of customers and traffic shifted to an emergency pool. We expect normal service shortly. Contact support for help with high-priority workflows."

maya: closing handoff. leaving logs and commands in the incident ticket.

ajay: last check: p95 stable 380ms, queue 1.1k, closing the immediate danger. Will keep monitoring and update when back to baseline.

ops-bot: Incident status: mitigated. next steps: quota request, autoscaler logic PR, runbook updates.

maya: filing RFC for autoscaler quota detection and pre-warm logic.

ajay: thanks everyone. I'll run a 2h watch and then move to followups.

(small emoji thread)

maya: :thumbsup:

ajay: :coffee:
